chapters.title: A Perpetual Motion Machine for Returns
chapters.sourcePressure: Tom Murphy and Capital Cities Broadcasting show how a smaller broadcaster compounded by joining lean headquarters, local operating responsibility, disciplined capital allocation, and patience for the rare major bet such as ABC.
chapters.coreMove: Treat overhead, local authority, and capital reserves as one compounding system instead of three separate management choices.
chapters.commonMisread: The weak version is generic thrift or decentralization cheerleading; the real pressure is whether every saved layer keeps judgment and cash available for higher-return use.

chapters.title: An Unconventional Conglomerateur
chapters.sourcePressure: Henry Singleton and Teledyne demonstrate fixed loyalty to per-share value while tactics shift from equity-funded acquisitions to large repurchases as valuation and market conditions change.
chapters.coreMove: Separate the permanent scorecard from the temporary instrument, then change instruments when facts and valuation change.
chapters.commonMisread: The weak version is that being contrarian is valuable by itself; Singleton is odd only because conventional behavior failed the per-share value test.

chapters.title: The Turnaround
chapters.sourcePressure: Bill Anders and General Dynamics show outsider discipline inside a damaged enterprise where portfolio triage and rational downsizing matter more than preserving inherited scale.
chapters.coreMove: Rank inherited assets by recovery value, then cut even proud pieces when they weaken the company that must survive.
chapters.commonMisread: The weak version is turnaround toughness or slash-and-burn cost cutting; the real test is contraction tied to future strength.

chapters.title: Value Creation in a Fast-Moving Stream
chapters.sourcePressure: John Malone and TCI show value creation in cable through structural intelligence, leverage, acquisition-shaped growth, and tax-aware design in a messy fast-changing industry.
chapters.coreMove: Judge complexity by retained value after financing, tax, and industry structure rather than by whether the plan looks clean.
chapters.commonMisread: The weak version praises complicated deals; the real pressure is whether the structure makes economics clearer and stronger instead of hiding weak economics.

chapters.title: The Widow Takes the Helm
chapters.sourcePressure: Katharine Graham and The Washington Post Company show reluctant succession turning into disciplined capital allocation and stewardship under public scrutiny.
chapters.coreMove: Convert inherited authority into earned stewardship by making clearer decisions before confidence fully arrives.
chapters.commonMisread: The weak version is an inspirational confidence story; the real pressure is title without automatic judgment and authority earned through stewardship.

chapters.title: A Public LBO
chapters.sourcePressure: Bill Stiritz and Ralston Purina show public-market management run with private-owner discipline, pruning unrelated operations and tightening focus around sharper economics.
chapters.coreMove: Make a public company answer owner-like economic tests by forcing sprawl, side bets, and operating softness to justify their capital.
chapters.commonMisread: The weak version is private-equity worship or harshness for style; the real pressure is focus plus operating rigor inside a public company.

chapters.title: Optimizing the Family Firm
chapters.sourcePressure: Dick Smith and General Cinema show capital allocation discipline inside family-control realities, where continuity can protect patience or shelter weak habits.
chapters.coreMove: Keep continuity useful by auditing protected habits harder than ordinary ones and making family-control advantages earn their place.
chapters.commonMisread: The weak version romanticizes family firms or attacks tradition; the real pressure is optimization under protection.

chapters.title: The Investor as CEO
chapters.sourcePressure: Warren Buffett and Berkshire Hathaway show the cleanest fusion of operator and investor logic: decentralized operating trust governed by central capital allocation judgment.
chapters.coreMove: Let operators run their businesses while the center keeps strict ownership of capital allocation, trust, and long-range value judgment.
chapters.commonMisread: The weak version is Buffett celebrity or stock-picking lore; the real pressure is investor logic as the operating system of a decentralized holding company.

chapters.title: Radical Rationality
chapters.sourcePressure: The synthesis chapter distills the outsider mind-set across Murphy, Singleton, Anders, Malone, Graham, Stiritz, Smith, and Buffett without flattening them into one tactic.
chapters.coreMove: Carry the value scorecard across contexts while forcing every admired tactic to re-earn its place under current facts.
chapters.commonMisread: The weak version is a formula or manifesto; the real pressure is principle over tactic while preserving case-specific differences.
mustNotDriftInto: all cases are basically the same
